Improving how electricity works for people and communities in the NWT
Yellowknife— April 17, 2025
New direction issued to the Public Utilities Board (PUB) will modernize how electricity is regulated and delivered in the Northwest Territories. The changes are designed to support the growing pressure to transition to a lower-carbon economy, while maintaining an electricity system that is safe, secure, affordable, and reliable.
The direction includes 11 policy directives focused on improving and expanding net metering and independent power producer programs, implementing rate impact mitigation measures, mandating long-term integrated system planning, and making several necessary regulatory updates. Many of these issues are interrelated. As a package, these changes reflect years of the Government of the Northwest Territories’ (GNWT) research and aim to balance system costs with the benefits of increased community participation and renewable energy adoption.
This work responds to long-standing issues raised by utilities, communities, and residents, while creating more space for Northerners to generate their own renewable power and manage their energy costs. It will also better position Indigenous and community governments to advance renewable energy opportunities and support local economic development.
These issues were largely echoed by invested parties, partners, and the public during broad engagement conducted by the GNWT in 2023 on the renewal of the 2030 Energy Strategy. This  policy direction represents the GNWT’s steps towards a revised strategic approach to energy in order to meet the GNWT’s net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 commitments.
For more information, visithttps://www.inf.gov.nt.ca/en/services/energy/about-nwt-public-utilities-board
QUOTES
“These changes are about building an energy system that works for everyone—today and into the future. We are creating more space for communities and Indigenous governments to lead clean energy projects, while taking clear steps to protect affordability, improve fairness and create new opportunities for Northerners. Managing the energy transition requires thoughtful planning and practical action, and that’s what this direction delivers .”
Caroline Wawzonek, Minister Responsible for Strategic Infrastructure, Energy and Supply Chains

“The Public Utilities Board plays a vital role in ensuring our energy system is fair, transparent, and accountable. This direction gives the Board clear guidance to support long-term planning, balance rate impacts, and enable broader participation in renewable energy development. It reflects our responsibility to ensure the system evolves in a way that protects the public interest and responds to the needs of today’s and tomorrow’s ratepayers.”
Vince McKay, Minister Responsible for the Public Utilities Board
QUICK FACTS
The new direction includes 11 interrelated directives to support a modern, affordable, and low-carbon electricity system in the NWT.
Community renewable energy caps in diesel-powered communities will increase from 20% to 30%, with further flexibility if battery storage is used.
All self-generators connected to the grid must now participate in a regulated program to ensure fair treatment for everyone—either Net Metering or Independent Power Production.
Compensation for self-generators will be set by the Public Utilities Board and will reflect the actual value of their contribution to the grid, promoting fairness for all ratepayers.
The Net Metering Program will expand to allow larger commercial projects while maintaining the 15kW cap for residential customers.
A new, standardized Independent Power Producer program will prioritize Indigenous and community ownership and ensure transparency in power purchase agreements.
Fixed monthly charges can now be adjusted to better reflect actual fixed infrastructure costs, helping to stabilize rates for all users.
Electric vehicle chargers will now be considered part of regulated utility operations, enabling utilities to support EV infrastructure development.
New electric heating rate options will be considered to help residents in hydro-powered zones take advantage of surplus electricity and reduce GHG emissions.
A special “low water rate rider” fund will be created to better buffer electricity costs against the impacts of periodic droughts in our hydropower systems .

Impaired Driving
Drive Sober – Arrive Alive
Driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol is dangerous and illegal.
Driving sober is a choice that saves lives and keeps our communities safe. Impaired driving is a serious risk that has far-reaching consequences, both legally and personally. When you’re behind the wheel, being fully alert and free of impairment is essential.
Let’s make responsible choices and help ensure everyone arrives home alive.
Why Drive Sober?
Think before you get behind the wheel. Impaired driving increases the risk of accidents, putting lives in danger.
Drugs and alcohol can impair your ability to focus, react quickly, and make safe choices, putting everyone at risk. Even small amounts of alcohol, cannabis or other drugs affect reaction times and decision-making. Staying sober behind the wheel ensures your safety and the safety of others on the road.
Tips for Sober Driving
Plan Ahead:If you’re going out, make plans for a safe ride home.
Designate a Driver:Travel with someone who can stay sober to get everyone home safely.
Use Safe Transportation Options:Cabs, and public transit are reliable alternatives.
Non-Alcoholic Options:Enjoy gatherings without alcohol or cannabis—mocktails and other non-alcoholic beverages are a great alternative.
Understanding Impaired Driving Laws in the NWT
Impaired driving means operating a vehicle (including cars, trucks, vessels, snowmobiles, and off-road vehicles) while under the influence of drugs, alcohol, or both, compromising your ability to drive safely. Here’s what to know:
Territorial zero tolerance:In the NWT, novice drivers, drivers under 22, and certain commercial drivers must have no drugs or alcohol in their system. Any presence results in a license suspension.
Alcohol limits for all drivers:Drivers with blood alcohol at or exceeding .05% face a 24-hour suspension, increasing to 30 days for repeated offenses.Levels at .08% or more result in a 90-day suspension.
Drivers with blood alcohol at or exceeding .05% face a 24-hour suspension, increasing to 30 days for repeated offenses.
Levels at .08% or more result in a 90-day suspension.
Federal penalties:Under the Criminal Code, impaired driving may result in fines, driving prohibitions, or imprisonment.
Cannabis
Transporting cannabis:Consuming cannabis or having an open container in a vehicle is illegal. Cannabis must be stored in its original, sealed container or in a closed container not accessible to the driver or passengers.
Medical cannabis users:All drivers are subject to the same laws, regardless of medical cannabis exemptions.
How long should I wait after using cannabis before driving?Everyone’s reaction to cannabis varies. The safest choice is to avoid driving if you have recently consumed cannabis.

Please note, this information is a summary and does not replace the law. For full details, consult the Motor Vehicles Act, the Criminal Code, and Bill C-46 (An Act to amend the Criminal Code).

NTPC and NT Hydro Board - Public Expression of Interest
Public Appointments to the NWT Power Corporation and NT Hydro Corporation Board of Directors
The Government of Northwest Territories (GNWT) is seeking expressions of interest from members of the public in NWT who wish to be considered for appointment to the Boards of Directors of the Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC) and Northwest Territories Hydro Corporation (NT Hydro) (together, “the Corporations”) for a term of up to three years to oversee the overall governance and direct the business of the Corporations. The Board of Directors Chair and Vice Chair will also be selected from the pool of qualified candidates.
Background
NTPC and NT Hydro are GNWT Crown corporations. NTPC is a wholly owned subsidiary of NT Hydro, which in turn is owned 100 percent by the GNWT. Both corporations are established, structured, and operated in accordance with the Northwest Territories Power Corporation Act (NTPC Act) and the Northwest Territories Hydro Corporation Act (NT Hydro Act), and share a common Board of Directors. Directors are appointed pursuant to this legislation by the Minister responsible.
NT Hydro activities relate primarily to providing oversight of NTPC and any other NT Hydro subsidiaries.[1]Under the Northwest Territories Hydro Corporation Act, Directors appointed to the NTPC Board also serve on the NT Hydro Board, and in practice are also appointed to the Boards of NT Hydro subsidiaries. For further information on the NTPC operating environment, including service area, key assets and customer base, please seeNPTC Operating Environment.
NTPC is regulated by the NWT Public Utilities Board (PUB), a quasi-judicial regulator under the NWT Public Utilities Act. NPTC must seek PUB review prior to construction of large capital projects or before changing electricity rates.
Further information can be found on the NTPC website:https://www.ntpc.com/.
What We Are Looking For
For the past 9 years the Corporations’ Board of Directors has been comprised of senior GNWT managers.  As the activities of the Corporations can have a profound impact on many aspects of life in the NWT, the GNWT wishes to implement public Board appointments at this time to ensure that the Corporations’ Directors reflect the diverse perspectives and interests of NWT’s people.
NTPC is a complex, modern public utility providing an essential service that impacts the lives of virtually all NWT residents and businesses. It is facing a number of challenges including maintaining affordable and reliable power supply to customers, while ensuring key asset renewals are completed and territorial emissions commitments are achieved (see Attachment 1 for details). Navigating these challenges requires that its Directors’ individually and collectively provide a diverse compliment of skills and experience as summarized below.  Additional details regarding the skills and attributes can be found here at theBoard Directors Skills Matrix.
Personal abilities necessary for all directors
Demonstrated leadership abilities
Communication skills
Collaborative, ability to work actively in a team environment
Independence and integrity
Business competence
Technical skills that would benefit the Board*
Ability to think strategically and critically
Utility experience or experience with a regulated industry
Lived experience in NWT communities, including Indigenous knowledge and experience
Financial experience
Governance and committee experience, including public sector knowledge and civic literacy
*As broad representation is a priority for the GNWT the absence of a specific technical skill will not necessarily be a disqualifying factor.
The GNWT is looking for public members that can provide impartial representation without significant conflicts of interest. Candidates that work for or represent other governments or special interest groups in the NWT may be eliminated from consideration.
Board Responsibilities and What to Expect
Under the NTPC Act, the Minister must appoint between six and ten Directors to oversee the governance and direct the business of the Corporations. Two of these directors will be appointments from the GNWT public service to ensure that the interests of the shareholder, the GNWT, are represented on the Board.
High level responsibilities of the Corporations’ Directors include:
Overseeing the development and implementation of corporate strategies in response to periodic mandate or direction letters from the Minister.
Overseeing the performance of the Corporation, including accountability and reporting mechanisms.
Making recommendations to the Minister regarding the appointment of the President of the Corporations and assessing the performance of the President and CEO of the Corporations.
Providing support and advice to the Minister the Board Chair upon the Minister’s request, or when needed by the Boards.
Upon appointment, Directors will receive onboarding and orientation, including training to understand Director roles, responsibilities, accountabilities, public utility governance, and legal responsibilities.
Public Board members will receive honoraria and compensation for their time in accordance with Ministerial-approved rate schedules.[2]Existing compensation rates are under review by the Minister.
The Boards are required to meet a minimum of four times annually, however, members should be prepared to meet more often as well as participate in sub-committees.
How to Apply and the Process
If you wish to be considered for appointment, please provide a copy of a current resume, or equivalent, as well as a cover letter describing how you meet the skills and experience requirements. Alternative means of application will be considered upon request to accommodate special or particular needs.
Your application should indicate if you wish to be considered for the role of chair, vice-chair or committee chair.[3]Please also provide your community, regional or demographic representation if you feel comfortable doing so.  Potential conflicts of interest must also be identified.
The GNWT will be accepting applications until May 15, 2025.
Initial screening and interviews will be conducted by a committee of corporate and shareholder representatives. Qualified candidates may be required to meet with the Minister responsible to determine suitability. Successful candidates will be appointed to the Corporations’ Boards by the Minister.  The Minister has the authority to appoint Directors to the Board, through the EOI process or through any other means, and will also appoint a Chair and Vice Chair.
Applications should be sent to:nwtenergy@gov.nt.ca. Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions.

[1]NT Hydro currently has one other wholly owned subsidiary, NT Energy
[2]This does not include the two board members from the public service.
[3]Currently, there are two authorized sub-committees: Audit & Efficiency and Compensation & Governance

Nominee Support
Contacting NT Nominee Program Staff
Staff with the Northwest Territories Nominee Program (NTNP) are here to help you whenever we can! Nominees can contact the NTNP at any time about any issue, such as, but not limited to:
You have questions or concerns about eligibility and criteria for the NTNP;
You are an approved nominee, and your current work permit is going to expire, and you need a Work Permit Support Letter;
There are any changes to your employment relationship with your nominating Employer;
You are having issues with your nominating Employer;
You are having issues contacting Immigration Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) about your application for permanent residency; and/or
You have questions about the Memorandum of Understanding.
You can contact the NTNP by email,immigration@gov.nt.caor by telephone, 1-855-440-5450.
Employer-Driven & Francophone Streams Specific
Work Permit Support Letters – Employer Driven & Francophone Streams
If your temporary work permit expires before a decision is reached on your Permanent Residency Application, our office can issue you a Work Permit Support Letter. You can use this letter to apply for a new work permit that is employer-specific so you can continue working for the Employer that nominated you.
If you require this letter, please reach out to our office by emailingimmigration@gov.nt.camore than 30 days and up to six (6) months before the expiration of your current work permit.
Memorandum of Understanding for Approved Nominees - Employer Driven & Francophone Streams
The terms of the Memorandum of Understanding signed after a worker is nominated must be followed by all parties until the nominee learns the decision of their application for permanent residency.
The NTNP must be notified within 10 business days of any changes to the employment relationship, such as, but not limited to, a reduction of hours below 30 hours per week, resignation, termination, and temporary or permanent lay-off.
Amendments to a Nomination - Employer Driven & Francophone Streams
The NTNP must be notified by email (immigration@gov.nt.ca) immediately if any changes need to be made on a nomination certificate. The NTNP may request updated documents that support the changes, and some changes may require consultation prior to approval. These changes may include:
Change of address;
Change of name;
Change of marital status;
Adding a dependent;
Changing occupations (must consult with NTNP first); and/or
Changing Employer (must consult with NTNP first).
Business Stream Specific
Employment Standards Act
As employers in the Northwest Territories, applicants under the NTNP Business Stream are subject to theEmployment Standards Actand legislation. Knowing your role, rights and responsibilities is essential. Please reach out toEmployment Standardsdirectly by phone at 867-767-9351 ext.71469 or emailemployment_standards@gov.nt.ca
Business Performance Agreement
The Business Performance Agreement contains the terms under which the Business Stream applicant will execute their business plan. When a Business Performance Agreement is signed, the Department of Industry, Tourism and Investment will provide the Business Stream applicant with a letter of support for a two (2) year temporary work permit. When making an application for a temporary work permit, the applicant must provide the letter of support, their business plan and their signed Business Performance Agreement to the Government of Canada.
Work Permit Support Letter – Business Stream
If your temporary work permit expires before you have completed your Business Performance Agreement, or before a decision has been made on your Permanent Residency Application, our office can issue you a Work Permit Support Letter. You can use this letter to apply for a new work permit that allows you to continue operating your business.
If you require this letter, please get in touch with our office by emailingimmigration@gov.nt.camore than 30 days and up to six (6) months before your current work permit expires.
Amendments to a Nomination - Business Stream
The NTNP must be notified by email (immigration@gov.nt.ca) immediately if any changes need to be made to a nomination certificate. The NTNP may request updated documents supporting the changes; some changes require a consultation before approval. These changes may include:
Change of address;
Change of name;
Change of marital status;
Adding a dependent; and/or
Changing business operations (must consult with NTNP first).

The application intake period for the Northwest Territories Nominee Program closed at 5pm on March 6, 2025.
On March 11, 2025, following pre-screening, 90 applications will be selected for assessment at random. The Employer, the Nominee Applicant and/or the Authorized Representative will receive an email if their application is selected.
Applications that are not selected will stay in the intake queue until December 12, 2025. If a space becomes available due to application denials or withdrawals, the NTNP will select an application for assessment from the intake queue at random. Selected applications will be notified by email.
If you have questions, please contact 1(855) 440-5450 orimmigration@gov.nt.ca.
The Employer-Driven Stream is for employers who want to hire and nominate foreign nationals when there are no Canadians or Canadian Permanent Residents available. This stream helps employers hire critically needed and skilled workers, and helps workers achieve Canadian Permanent Residency through three program categories.
For this stream to work, you first need a job offer from an NWT employer and then have the NWT Employer apply to the program on your behalf.
To find a potential employer, try these websites, which list employment opportunities in the NWT:
Edge North Job Board
Canada Job Bank(search Northwest Territories)
GNWT Careers
Northern News Services Job Listings
Indeed Jobs - Northwest Territories

For the 2025 intake, there will be a set number of applications an NWT employer can submit to the Employer Driven Stream based on the size of their business.
Employers with 1-10 total NWT employees: 1 application
Employers with 11-49 total NWT employees: 2 applications
Employers with 50+ total NWT employees; 4 applications
How does this Stream work?
Once you have a job offer from an NWT employer, the employer will need to contact our team and apply for one of three program categories:

SKILLED WORKER

Department Information
The Department of Infrastructure (INF) provides high quality services to the public and Government of the Northwest Territories’ (GNWT) departments, boards and agencies including the planning, design, construction, acquisition, operation and maintenance of public transportation infrastructure and the buildings, works and equipment required for the GNWT to deliver its programs and services. Department Information
The Tlicho Community Services Agency is a unique organization responsible for the delivery of education, health and social services within the Tlicho region. The Tlicho Community Services Agency's vision 'Strong Like Two People' is a metaphor for the desire by community leadership to build an organization, and create programs and services that recognize the strength and importance of two cultures.
Job Information
At the discretion of the Principal, the Support Assistant reports to the Principal, Vice Principal, Program Support Teacher and/or Classroom Teachers. The position is responsible for assisting with implementing specialized and modified learning and education activities in order to provide a positive learning experience for students with special needs or students who require additional support. The SA is responsible for working with special needs/additional needs students either individually or in small groups to provide academic assistance in mainly core areas such as reading and math. The SA is also responsible for ensuring that special needs/additional needs students are provided with positive learning environments and have an opportunity to learn effective listening and communications skills and good work habits. In particular, the SA is responsible for assisting with implementation of Student Support Plan (SSP) so that students are provided with a learning environment that promotes a sense of accomplishment and self-confidence.
Providing these services in an adequate manner will have a direct impact on special needs/additional needs students and their families. It will increase the chances of having these students remain in the education system and gaining the skills required to be successful in life. It will also have a direct impact on the ability of the Classroom Teacher to maintain order in the classroom as many children with special needs may become frustrated and demonstrate inappropriate or disruptive behaviors in the classroom without special or additional assistance. Providing these services will also have a direct impact on other students within the classroom who may not otherwise receive the required level of attention from the Classroom Teacher.
The Support Assistant (SA) is responsible for assisting with instruction and providing support and encouragement to students diagnosed with special needs and/or who require additional attention in order to ensure all students have the opportunity for a successful and meaningful learning experience. The SA operates under the Education Act and the policies and procedures established by the district, region and school.
Typically, the qualifications for the position would be attained by:
The Completion of Grade 12 combined with related training in working with special needs students and experience in an educational environment.
Relevant experiences include:
Day camp worker for students under 18
Daycare worker
Camp counsellor
Coach for students under 18
Substitute teacher
The incumbent must have or be prepared to obtain First Aid and CPR Certification.
An ability to speak the local Aboriginal Language and knowledge of sign language is considered a strong asset for this position.

Regional Recruitment Program

What is the Regional Recruitment Program?
What funding is available for the Regional Recruitment Program?
How do I apply for the Regional Recruitment Program?
Resources
What is the Regional Recruitment Program?
The Regional Recruitment Program is a recruitment and on-the-job training program that links vacant regional positions to potential candidates by providing financial and human resource support to departments, boards and agencies.
On-the-job training focuses on the unique competencies of each individual trainee by implementing training plans and mentorship for the duration of their on-the-job training experience.
What funding is available for the Regional Recruitment Program?
Up to $15,000 per trainee position is provided through the Regional Recruitment Program. The number of available funded positions varies each year and is dependent on the number of trainee positions that require maximum funding. This is how trainee positions are funded:
Trainees are paid at 80% of the position’s full salary (in accordance with the Trainee Provisions in the UNW Collective Agreement). The remaining 20% of the position’s salary is used by departments, boards or agencies to support the trainee’s individual training and development.
To further support the department and trainee, up to $15,000 per position is provided through the RRP. This funding supports additional training and development costs above the salary and O&M funding already in place for the vacant position.
An additional training allowance up to $6,000 per annum per trainee is available through the RRP for on-the-job training to the trainee, as outlined in the training plan.
How do I apply for the Regional Recruitment Program?
A hiring manager must submit an application to the Regional Recruitment Specialist. Applications are received and assessed year-round and departments are welcome to submit an application at any time.

The Public Health Nurse (PHN) reports directly to the Nurse in Charge (NIC), in Behchoko. The PHN provides culturally sensitive care to people in the remote community of Behchoko and is critical to ensuring the health of the community. The PHN has in-depth knowledge of the Public Health Act and the Reportable Disease Control and Disease Surveillance Regulations. The position works directly with the NWT Department of Health and Social Service's (DHSSs) Communicable Disease Specialists in the Office of the Chief Public Health Officer (OCPHO). The PHN has an essential role in the timely identification of communicable diseases and the delivery of prevention and outbreak management and control interventions, especially in the areas of vaccine delivery, communicable disease surveillance and treatment.

Department Information
The Northwest Territories Health and Social Services Authority (NTHSSA) offers challenging and exciting careers in health and social services delivery and administration in Canada’s North. The Territorial Authority has service locations in communities across the territory and a staff of more than 1,600 serving over 43,000 residents of the NWT and 5,900 residents of the Kitikmeot Region of Nunavut.  Challenging work, welcoming communities, and expanded opportunities are some of the benefits offered to employees of the NTHSSA.
Job Information
The Northwest Territories Health and Social Services Authority (NTHSSA) is seeking a skilled and compassionate Nurse in Charge (NIC) to oversee the operations of the Long Term Care (LTC) facility at the Fort Simpson Health Centre. This facility provides long-term, respite, and palliative care to individuals, primarily seniors, who require 24-hour nursing support in a culturally respectful and home-like environment.
Reporting to the Regional Manager of Continuing Care Services, the NIC plays a vital leadership role by managing the day-to-day clinical operations of the LTC facility while also providing hands-on nursing care. The successful candidate will be responsible for directing and mentoring a multidisciplinary team of healthcare and support staff, coordinating individualized care plans, and ensuring that care delivery aligns with current standards of practice and the policies of the NTHSSA. This role also involves close collaboration with families, physicians, allied health professionals, and community resources to ensure residents receive holistic, person-centered care.
To succeed in this role, candidates must be Registered Nurses in good standing with the ability to apply nursing theory and practice in a clinical leadership setting. Strong knowledge of long-term care nursing and continuing care principles is essential. Candidates must demonstrate the ability to supervise and support a team, communicate effectively, and operate both medical and non-medical equipment used in resident care. Proficiency in using digital tools such as word processing software and email is expected. The ideal applicant will also bring a commitment to confidentiality, experience working in culturally diverse settings, and a genuine desire to improve the health and quality of life for residents in a northern community.
This is a meaningful opportunity to live and work in a welcoming and close-knit community while making a real difference in the lives of residents. The Northwest Territories offers a unique lifestyle, competitive compensation, and the chance to be part of a healthcare system that values excellence, accountability, and respect for regional diversity.
Typically, the qualifications for this position are attained through the successful completion of a Nursing Degree, 3 years recent nursing experience in a long-term care setting and 1-year supervisory experience. Within the NTHSSA nurses must be registered with the RNANT-NU and have completed a satisfactory criminal record check.
